text:
rebecca: Heads up — we started seeing intermittent pod-to-pod packet loss in the us-east-2 GPU backfill pool around 09:10 UTC. GRPC calls hit timeouts and we see retried shards. Roughly 0.2-0.6% packet loss on short-lived flows.

sam: saw same on host logs. tcp_retransmits and out-of-order acks spike during 10-30s windows. quick tcpdump from worker-23 attached (paste below).

rebecca: ```
09:12:03.123456 IP 10.2.5.12.34567 > 10.2.6.34.443: Flags [P.], seq 1234:1678, ack 987, win 64240
... (repeated dup acks, retransmits)
---
eth0: RX dropped 128 TX dropped 0
vxlan0: RX dropped 120
```

jon: can you run iperf3 UDP and TCP between the two pods? curious if it's pure loss or reorder/fragmentation.

infra-bot: detected correlated increase in overlay drops across 8 hosts in us-east-2 between 09:05-09:18 UTC. Related alerts: overlay-pktloss-high (8 hosts), pod-grpc-failures (12 pods).

sam: iperf3 TCP between pod-a -> pod-b: bandwidth fine, but TCP retransmits spike under 100 concurrent streams. iperf3 UDP shows ~0.5% loss when sending 9k payloads.

vivian: my first suspicion is VXLAN fragmentation + NIC offloads (GRO/GSO) interacting badly when outer/inner MTU mismatch occurs. We've hit similar with mlx5 + kernel 5.15 where fragments get coalesced incorrectly and then dropped by offload. Any recent kernel or NIC firmware updates on these nodes?

rebecca: no recent firmware changes. nodes are on kube-1.25 with kernel 5.15.21-default. We do have jumbo MTU enabled (9000) on host overlay, but some nodes showing 1500 on underlying eth0 after a recent rolling maintenance — maybe an MTU mismatch during upgrade.

jon: that would explain frag/oo. quick probe: run `sudo ethtool -k eth0` and `ip link show` on the failing hosts. Also `dmesg | grep -i vxlan` to see driver complaints.

sam: ran checks, found 2 hosts (worker-23, worker-47) with eth0 mtu 1500 while vxlan0 mtu is 9000. small-window backfills hit those hosts more.

vivian: workaround we can try immediately: disable GRO/GSO on the host NICs to force the kernel to handle segmentation. command: `sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off` — will increase CPU but should stop pathological coalescing that leads to drops. We can roll as a daemonset if it fixes it.

rebecca: applied ethtool on worker-23 and worker-47. immediate improvement: packet loss dropped from ~0.45% to ~0.02%. GRPC timeouts subsided. CPU for kube-proxy bumped ~8%.

ops-lead: good mitigation. schedule a controlled daemonset to toggle off GRO/GSO on affected kernel versions + nodes that show MTU mismatch. Also open a ticket with cloud infra to reconcile host MTU during rolling upgrades.

jon: long-term options: pin MTU across fleet, enforce preflight node configuration, or upgrade NIC firmware/kernel that fixes mlx5 offload frag handling. Also consider enabling path MTU discovery probes (`sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1`) in case PMTU blackhole is happening.

vivian: note: we must be careful with blanket GRO/GSO off on all nodes — performance hit for steady high-throughput pods. Plan: target only nodes with mismatched MTU or kernel versions <= 5.15.21 and have a CPU guardrail. I can prototype a node-exporter rule and alert if tx/rx drops > 0.1% after the change.

rebecca: rolling daemonset (patch) applied to 15 nodes in the affected AZ with a 5m canary. so far 12/15 show drop improvement, 3 with no change (further investigation).

sam: follow-up trace on one of the non-improved hosts shows RDMA path fallback triggers (we use rdma on some GPU hosts). RDMA verbs are sensitive to offloads; disabling GRO there had no effect because the drop appears earlier on the RDMA stack. opened a separate ticket to debug RDMA path.

infra-bot: action items created: INFRA-2314 (daemonset GRO/GSO mitigation), INFRA-2315 (host MTU reconciliation), INFRA-2316 (RDMA path investigation).

ops-lead: assign owners and ETA for Infra-2315 by EOD. we need to avoid rolling upgrades causing MTU drift.

rebecca: postmortem draft: https://go/internal/infra/pm/2026-03-vxlan-frag-mismatch — will add timelines and mitigations.

vivian: final note — if you hit similar in other regions, do not escalate full fleet change; target AZs with confirmed MTU mismatch first. We'll propose an automated preflight to validate MTU before any node reimage. :white_check_mark:

rebecca: thanks everyone — will follow up once RDMA ticket has more details.
